blocking.section: Decision outcome (Limits row, line 51); Figure 1 (node lim, line 66)
blocking.issue: The Limits row applies complexity to every operation. That contradicts the owning document, where complexity applies in federation mode only and pass-through uses a field-count limit. It also contradicts this ADR's own Context (line 19).
blocking.evidence: Line 51: "| Limits | Depth, alias and complexity checks run per normalized operation before any subgraph call, with the Multi-protocol defaults; settings are OQ-multi-protocol-5 |". Line 19: "pass-through, which forwards each operation to one `graphql` Upstream under depth, alias and field-count limits". 07-multi-protocol.md, Depth, complexity and persisted queries: "| Complexity | ... federation mode only | 5,000 points (target) |"; Engine: "Pass-through mode ... enforcing syntax, depth, alias and field-count limits".
blocking.fix: Replace the rule cell with: "Depth and alias limits in both modes, field count in pass-through mode and complexity in federation mode only, run per operation after fragment expansion and before any subgraph call, with the Multi-protocol defaults; settings are OQ-multi-protocol-5". Relabel Figure 1 node `lim` as "Ruralz depth, alias, field-count and complexity checks".

blocking.section: Decision drivers (Runtime configuration, line 27); Decision outcome (Federation row, line 50)
blocking.issue: The ADR treats the GraphQL schema and supergraph as Revision content and states the supergraph source as a settled rule. `02-configuration-model.md` defines no schema, supergraph or subgraph field: GraphQL appears only as `Route.spec.match.graphql` (`operationType`, `operationName`) and `Upstream.spec.protocol: graphql`. OQ-multi-protocol-4 is still open and Blocking for federation, with option (c) only proposed. The owning document says federation "would" plan against an external supergraph. An accepted ADR that writes the proposed option as a rule, and implies Revision content that the Configuration model does not define, goes further than the binding sources allow.
blocking.evidence: Line 27: "**Runtime configuration**: a Revision, not a rebuilt binary, carries schemas and Routes, and Hot Reload activates it (P5)." Line 50: "| Federation | Plans against a supergraph SDL composed outside Ruralz and pinned by digest, since v2 has no composition package (OQ-multi-protocol-4) |". Owning doc, Engine: "Federation mode would plan against a supergraph SDL composed outside Ruralz and pinned by digest (OQ-multi-protocol-4)". OQ-multi-protocol-4 options: "(a) A `federation` composition mode; (b) `Route.spec.graphql` fields; (c) An external supergraph pinned by digest (proposed); (d) Composition in Ruralz Control".
blocking.fix: Line 27: "**Runtime configuration**: a Revision, not a rebuilt binary, carries Routes and, once OQ-multi-protocol-4 decides how they are declared, subgraph and supergraph schemas; Hot Reload activates it (P5)." Line 50: "Would plan against a supergraph SDL composed outside Ruralz and pinned by digest, the proposed option (c) of OQ-multi-protocol-4, since v2 has no composition package; the declaring field is not yet in the Configuration model". Add to More information a Proposed amendment that OQ-multi-protocol-4 also covers the pass-through schema source, if pass-through validates operations against one. Do not name a field.

blocking.issue: The ADR accepts that a supergraph could pass `ruralz bundle validate` and still fail as a Node NACK. This breaks the Configuration model's validation contract. Validation and diff semantics guarantees that a Bundle passing `ruralz bundle validate` passes the offline stages of Node activation with identical diagnostics, and it lists exactly five checks that can still fail afterward (RZ-CFG-028, -033, -024, -026, -027). A planner-only rejection would be a sixth. The tech stack Dependency graph also states that GraphQL document errors "surface in `ruralz bundle validate`, not as Node NACKs". The ADR's own driver (line 29) promises the same errors in all three binaries.
blocking.evidence: Line 88: "a supergraph that only the planner rejects may surface as a Node NACK rather than a `ruralz bundle validate` error." 02-configuration-model.md: "a Bundle that passes `ruralz bundle validate` in CI passes the offline stages of Ruralz Control ingest and Node activation with identical diagnostics ... After a green offline run, five checks can still fail". Tech stack: "such errors surface in `ruralz bundle validate`, not as Node NACKs (size cost: OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-22)". Line 29: "`ruralz`, `ruralz-control` and `ruralzd` report the same GraphQL errors".
blocking.fix: Keep the contract. Let `ruralz-control` and `ruralz` also link `engine/plan` for supergraph planning checks only (never `engine/resolve`, datasources or `subscription`), update the ruralz-control/ruralz row and the Confirmation checklist item to match, and replace the Bad clause with "and planning checks add `engine/plan` to Ruralz Control and the CLI (size: OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-22)". If that is rejected, add a Proposed amendment asking the Configuration model to register a sixth post-offline failure with its RZ-CFG code through an Open question, and mark the gap as pending that amendment instead of accepting it silently.

blocking.issue: Figure 1 contradicts the Phase mapping in the owning document in three ways. (1) The whole Filter Chain is one box before parsing and normalization, but the owning document runs `onRequestBody` on the normalized operation and `onUpstreamRequest` per subgraph fetch, after planning. (2) Subscriptions go `wrap --> sub --> ds` and skip normalization, the limits and `engine/plan`, but the owning document requires each `subscribe` to run `onRequestBody`, the checks and per-subgraph `onUpstreamRequest`. (3) No upstream-leg Phase appears between `ds` and `up`, although the Transport row and Good consequence 2 depend on it.
blocking.evidence: Line 75: `gw --> fc --> wrap --> norm --> lim --> plan --> res --> ds --> up`; line 76: `wrap --> sub --> ds`. Owning doc Figure 2: "onRequestHeaders, then onRequestBody on the normalized operation"; Subscriptions: "each `subscribe` is proposed to run `onRequestBody`, the checks below and per-subgraph `onUpstreamRequest`"; Filter Chain applicability: `onRequestBody` "Normalized operation", `onUpstreamRequest` "Per subgraph fetch" and "Per subgraph subscription".
blocking.fix: Redraw with nodes such as: `fcreq["onRequestHeaders"]` before `norm`; `fcbody["onRequestBody on the normalized operation"]` between `norm` and `lim`; `leg["upstream leg: onUpstreamRequest per subgraph fetch or subscription"]` between `ds` and `up`. Route subscriptions as `sub --> norm` (per `subscribe`, OQ-multi-protocol-17), so they share `norm`, `fcbody`, `lim` and `plan`. Keep the diagram at or under 25 nodes and update the caption.

blocking.section: Decision outcome (Advisory floor row, line 53); Confirmation (Advisory floor, line 97)
blocking.issue: The milestone tag conflicts with the roadmap and with when the module arrives. The explicit gorilla/websocket `require` is tagged Planned (M0), but graphql-go-tools, the only module that brings gorilla/websocket in, lands with GraphQL at M3 (the roadmap M3 row: "GraphQL module, limits and transport in `ruralzd`, `ruralz-control` and `ruralz`"). The verifier flags the line.
blocking.evidence: Line 53: "| Advisory floor | Explicit `require` of `gorilla/websocket` v1.5.3 over the v1.5.1 pin ... | Planned (M0) |". Line 97: "**Advisory floor**, Planned (M0): the explicit `require` holds `gorilla/websocket` at v1.5.3 or newer". Verifier: "WARN milestones docs/adr/0012-graphql-engine-graphql-go-tools.md:97 'Advisory floor, : the explicit require' is Planned (M0) but has no matching item under the M0 section of docs/roadmap/01-roadmap-and-milestones.md".
blocking.fix: Retag both as Planned (M3), "in the pull request that first adds graphql-go-tools to `go.mod`". Keep `govulncheck` on every pull request, Planned (M0), per Update policy, as the mechanism that enforces the floor once the module is linked.

blocking.issue: The ADR misstates the tech stack Admission mechanism. Admission (tech stack Figure 3) checks G1, G2, G3, govulncheck and a catalog row. It has no step that rejects modules listed in Alternatives not chosen, whose "Never" is a value in the "Revisit if" column, not a gate. gqlgen, bramble and graphql-go are MIT and pure Go, so Admission as written would admit them. The confirmation mechanism the ADR names does not exist.
blocking.evidence: Line 95: "gqlgen, bramble and graphql-go are listed \"Never\" under [Alternatives not chosen](...), so [Admission](...) rejects them." Tech stack Alternatives not chosen header: "| Alternative | Concern | Why not chosen | Revisit if | Source |" with "Never" in Revisit if. Admission: "A new direct dependency MUST get a catalog row in the same pull request."
blocking.fix: Rewrite as: "**Dependency admission**, Planned (M0): the GraphQL catalog row cites this ADR, and a depguard banned-import rule for `github.com/99designs/gqlgen`, `github.com/movio/bramble` and `github.com/graphql-go/graphql` (Proposed amendment to Repository layout and conventions) fails any pull request that imports them." Add that rule to the depguard amendment in More information.

blocking.issue: The driver claims gates G1 to G3, and the tech stack requires every dependency to pass all three. The ADR assesses G1 and G2 but says nothing about G3, the crypto denylist behind the FIPS build (`GOFIPS140`, pack section 1). No Confirmation item covers it, even though graphql-go-tools pulls in two WebSocket libraries and connect.
blocking.evidence: Line 28: "**Gates G1 to G3** and criteria S1, S2, S6 and S7". Line 84: "so it passes G2, S1 and S2; G1 awaits the CI cross-build." Line 96: "**G1 cross-build and license gate**, Planned (M0): confirm pure Go and MIT over the linked package set." Tech stack Selection criteria: "| G3 | Cryptographic primitives come only from Go `crypto/...` ... | `go list -deps` crypto denylist in CI, Planned (M0); FIPS CI job, Planned (M5) |".
blocking.fix: End line 84 with "; G1 and G3 await the CI cross-build and crypto denylist". Change line 96 to "**G1 cross-build, G3 crypto denylist and license gate**, Planned (M0), plus the FIPS CI job, Planned (M5): confirm pure Go, Go-module-only cryptography and MIT over the linked package set including graphql-go-tools".

non_blocking.suggestion: OQ-tech-stack-and-libraries-6 asks only about "Two JOSE stacks (jwx, go-jose via go-oidc)". Tech stack Selection criteria attaches the gorilla/websocket S6 exception to it, but the OQ row does not cover it. Link [Selection criteria](../engineering/01-tech-stack-and-libraries.md#selection-criteria) for the accepted exception, and add a Proposed amendment asking the tech stack to widen OQ-6 or open a WebSocket-specific OQ.

The row matches the tech stack catalog ("import only `ast` and `astvalidation`"). It conflicts with tech stack Figure 2 ("graphql-go-tools parser and validation") and with research, where lexer and parser are separate packages from `ast` (see L1-1). Add a Proposed amendment so the tech stack aligns its catalog row with its Figure 2, and use the same wording in this ADR.

The owning document's Limits row also bounds subgraph bodies "within `maxResponseBodyBytes`" together. Name both Gateway `limits` fields, `maxBufferedBytes` and `maxResponseBodyBytes`, so the driver matches the owning document.

Research records only that Kong's GraphQL Rate Limiting Advanced page has "no federation mention". Rephrase "Kong documents only an Enterprise GraphQL rate-limiting plugin" to "Kong's researched GraphQL plugin is the Enterprise GraphQL Rate Limiting Advanced, with no federation mention".

krakend-parity.md lists GraphQL as available in both KrakenD editions, without federation. "GraphQL forwarded as plain HTTP ... as in KrakenD" misdescribes KrakenD's GraphQL support. Write "with no federation, which KrakenD lacks in either edition".
ADR-0009 never mentions GraphQL. Describe it as "(the `net/http` and quic-go listeners)" rather than "(the listeners that carry GraphQL)".

The body is about 1,310 words by the manifest word_count_rule, against the 1,500 maximum. Pay for the fixes by merging the option 1 pros and cons, which repeat Consequences, and do not cut the Rules table.
